record.file_problem: Only the README and file list were provided; linked documents and result files are listed but their contents are not included.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports a weight-edit intervention on refusal-related directions and its effects on harmful-request compliance and capability, but describes a layer-local SRA Householder edit rather than the original all-layer, all-position activation projection.
record.gate_note: The README reports outcomes for a layer-local refusal-subspace edit on DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731. Script names, listed documents, and artifacts not described with outcomes are not treated as results.
record.test_reason: The project turns a refusal direction into a weight edit on the released DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 and reports harmful-request compliance and capability before and after. That bears on V2 (abliteration of a released model). The direction is capability-PC-cleaned (SRA) and per-layer. It is applied to wo_b in layers 10–42 as a strength-2 Householder reflection (flip), not projection. So it does not test V1's ablation of a plain difference-in-means direction.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right: the authors present a validated, reversible refusal-subspace weight edit. It raises harmful-request compliance to 90.59% (and 10/10 on a probe) and passes their capability gate of losing no more than 3 points. They frame it as an engineering release, not a test of the single-direction hypothesis.
record.recipe_differences: This is a repo/tool project, not a stated reproduction of the original study. It captures last-prefill-token activations, derives per-layer refusal directions and capability-PC-cleaned SRA alternatives, and applies a layer-local rank-1 Householder weight edit to attention wo_b in layers 10–42. It does not report the original all-layer, all-position activation projection.
record.method_sensitivity: The candidate is layer-local and uses layers 10–42; the README says it swept global versus layer-local directions, layer ranges, edit strength, row-norm preservation, and MTP handling, but does not report comparative outcomes for those settings.
record.problems: Evidence is presented as README summaries; the supplied text does not include the underlying evaluation protocols or linked reports. The harmful-request behavior audit has 85 prompts, and the separate bilingual harmful probe has 10 prompts. No uncertainty is stated for those behavior results.
record.rows_left_out: None. Other linked documents and result artifacts are listed but their contents and additional outcomes are not present in the supplied text.

relationships.condition: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, layer-local SRA rank-1 Householder reflection on wo_b in layers 10–42
relationships.reason: Compliance rose 3.53%→90.59% (r1) and 0/10→10/10 (r2). Harmless refusals did not increase (r3), and HumanEval, GSM8K, MMLU-Pro and writing stayed close to source (r4–r7).
relationships.display_finding: Compliance rose from 3.53% to 90.59% and from 0/10 to 10/10, while harmless refusals did not increase and HumanEval, GSM8K, MMLU-Pro and writing stayed close to source performance.

relationships.condition: Edit choice: reflection (strength 2) of a capability-cleaned direction, with layers selected by sweep
relationships.reason: Removal was reported only for a swept, modified edit (reflection, SRA cleaning, layers 10–42), not plain ablation. About 9% of the 85 audit prompts were still not complied with (r1).
relationships.display_finding: The reported result used SRA cleaning and reflection across layers 10–42, yet about 9% of 85 audit prompts still received no compliant answer.
